title: Tangkhul Folk Literature Anthology
title_translation: Anthology of Tangkhul Folklore, Ballads, and Proverbs
creator: S. Arokianathan
author: S. Arokianathan
publisher: Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysore
notes: Seminal scholarly anthology published under CIIL Folklore Series documenting Tangkhul oral narratives, courting songs, funeral dirges, proverbs, and riddles with linguistic commentary.
indigenous_tangkhul_text: Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL) Mysore-na 1982-li Tangkhul Folk Literature monograph publish sakya.
Dr. S. Arokianathan-na oral narratives, folk ballads (Maitonphi), dirges, riddles, kala proverbs document sakya.
Phonetic transcription, English translations, kala structural linguistic analysis comprehensive-laka sanga.
english_translation_text: In 1982, the Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL) in Mysore published this definitive Tangkhul Folk Literature monograph.
Compiled by Dr. S. Arokianathan, it systematically documented oral tales, the ballad of Maitonphi, proverbs, and riddles.
Featuring IPA phonetic transcriptions and interlinear English translations, it remains a landmark of academic linguistic folklore.
literary_themes: Comprehensive scientific documentation of oral literature genres
Preservation of archaic dialects (Phungcham, Ukhrul, Champhung)
Linguistic, metric, and syntactic analysis of traditional verbal art
structure_and_meter: Multilingual scholarly monograph containing bilingual texts, phonetic notations, structural tables, and glossaries.
critical_commentary: The premier academic anthology of Tangkhul oral verbal art, establishing standard methodology for Tibeto-Burman folklore documentation.

poetic_vocabulary_terms.Folk-Literature: Indigenous oral lore, verbal art, and narrative tradition
poetic_vocabulary_terms.Paochirun: Traditional poetic riddles and witty word-games
poetic_vocabulary_terms.Khararchan-Laa: Ballad poetry set to traditional melodies
